newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bremen cotton buyers seek early 1997 supply.
newsitem.headline: Bremen cotton buyers seek early 1997 supply.

text.p: European spinning mills made enquiries for early 1997 shipment dates, the Bremen Cotton Exchange's fortnightly report said on Monday.
New crop upland cottons of differing origins were little changed in price despite worsening crop prospects in Pakistan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan and Greece, it noted.
Poorer harvests in these countries might be offset by higher results in the U.S. and India.
But uncertainty about the final balance for the current supply and demand balance blocked trades for distant shipment dates.
Bremen cotton stocks were reduced by 1,149 bales in the fortnight ended Nov 1 to 34,316 bales, which compared with 43,932 bales recorded a year earlier.

In the upland sector, the Exchange reported spot through first half 1997 sales of Central Asian cotton standards 1 and 2 and U.S. MOT, sales of West African descriptions for spot and first quarter 1997, Greek medium grades for first quarter only and Indian Deshi for December through March.
Mexican low grades traded for November 1996 and Chad cotton for first through third quarter 1997.
It also reported long staple sales in Egyption Giza 77 and U.S.-Pima for first quarter 1997 as well as spot Central Asian and Sudan-Barakat transactions.
